message: player_3, one thing your Sentinel claim doesn't actually settle: a watch result never includes the watcher, so \"no one visited player_4\" is exactly what your own watch would look like whether or not you went to player_4 — the only way we resolve this is that words never lie in that direction, so the follow by player_4 has to be checked against a second sighting. The real problem I want an answer on: both of you claim to have sat on the same door, and one of those abilities has a limit of two uses. player_3, did you hold your second watch or place it somewhere else? That answer will show up if we can test it.

Two players have abstained both days and said almost nothing: player_6 and player_9. With a necromancer alive and someone dead whose role is hidden, the quiet abstainer is exactly where I'd look. player_6, who would you vote for today and why? I'd start there.

Worth putting on the table: I followed player_9 last night and they went to player_4 — the same player who got sigil-struck. A real investigator check fits that, so player_9's claim is holding up better than I expected. Anyone want to own up to visiting player_4? Whoever hit them with the sigil should speak up, since that's our one confirmed wolf dead and your note is the last clear line we have.

The wording slip matters less than the sequencing: player_4 described a visitor at his own door before ever naming a follow, so the 'player_3 visited player_4' line reads like it was reverse-engineered after player_3 pushed back. Still, a real Trailseer would see exactly that phrasing, so I want a second result from player_4 tonight before I weigh player_3's denial as strong. Those two are the pair to sort.

One thing nobody's flagged: a follow tells you where the target went, and player_4 says the result was \"player_3 visited player_4\" — that's the shape of a watch on player_4's own door, which the Trailseer can't do. Either player_4 is misreporting the wording or is really a Sentinel claiming Trailseer. player_3's claim of no visiting role is the easier half to check, but player_4's story needs to be said exactly.

New info I'm sitting on: player_9, whose body is hidden, did go to player_4 the night player_4 got struck by a sigil. That's a real visit from the hidden corpse, so whoever player_9 was, their claim wasn't just talk — don't lynch blind over that. The more interesting question is why the wolves hid that specific body instead of showing it.

You're right, and that's the honest answer: I had no checks left, so I held on night 3. I said out loud I *planned* to check player_5, not that I had — so you following me and seeing nothing is exactly what should have happened. Which night I'm checking from here? None. I'm out of checks; my night-2 read was Not suspicious on player_8.

Straight answer to you, player_10: I had no checks left, so night 3 I held — that's you seeing nothing at my door, consistent. I never claimed a night-3 result; my last check went on player_8 on night 2. Note player_3's watch and player_5's will both put player_5 at me on night 2, which is the one watch line that's actually checkable.

player_4, I'm not dropping the player_7 point — it was never about silence. My reasoning is mechanical: our kill last night plainly failed to land, and the only body that shrugs off a kill on night 1 is the Necromancer. That's a living problem the pack can't solve at night, so it's ours to solve in daylight. Your follow and player_3's watch are a wording fight with no proof either way; the immunity logic is the one thing that's actually testable. If I'm wrong, a real Sentinel or Trailseer can name who they saw touching a door.

I've been holding this back but it needs saying now: I'm the Trailseer, and last night I followed player_1 — they targeted player_3, who was killed by the wolves that same night. That's a claim I can put to the Sentinel-type check or the Healer's record; someone at the table can verify the visitor pattern. player_8 is the other half: my reads and the roster narrow them to a killer role, and player_7's night-2 visit to player_8, which I saw myself, is the only confirmed trace linking a survivor to anything. I'd vote player_8 right now unless someone gives me a reason the night-4 visit from player_1 is benign.

That visit was me, and I'll say it plainly: I'm the Sentinel, and night 1 I watched you, player_4 — the result was nobody targeted you, so nobody attacked, checked, protected or blocked you. I can't see what you did, only that no one came to your door. What were you doing at my place, though? Because a track on me without a stated intent is exactly the shape of a wolf's Chanteuse/Illusionist visit, and last night is the one your claim actually needs to explain.

On the player_3/player_4 clash — there's a reading neither of you offered: a Trailseer's own watch never shows himself, so if player_3 visited player_4 by an ability, that visit being the thing player_4 saw is exactly what a follow result would show; the contradiction is in player_4's arrival framing. I'd want player_3 to say plainly what they did to player_4 last night before we vote.

Guilty — I targeted you last night, player_4, so your follow is accurate. My action resolved and I got my result, so nothing blocked me; I'll say what I was up to at the right time, but it isn't a kill on you. Any watcher on you would have seen me, which is worth noting.

The thing player_5 flagged is the whole game today: player_3 says he's the Sentinel who watched player_4, but if that's true, then player_3's own visit to player_4 should have shown up in his watch result — it came back empty. So either player_3 wasn't at that door (and his claim is a story), or he's not the Sentinel he says. Either way I'm leaning toward player_3 over player_4 right now. I'll say plainly: I'm the Healer, I protected player_10 last night, and I'd vote player_3 today.

I've been quiet, so let me put one concrete thread on the table. Last night player_3 died to the wolves — I'd like whoever visited player_3 to say so before we vote, because I have reason to believe someone did. player_1, what did you do last night? An honest answer narrows this down fast; a dodge doesn't.

player_4, my point stands and nothing you've said changes it: if your follow is real, you saw player_3 go somewhere, and that's a Trailseer result — fine, that's consistent now. But the reason I'd still test this is that the pack's kill vanished on night 1, and the only body it can't drop is the Necromancer. That means the person the wolves bit is standing in this circle right now. I want that seat found, not the wording argued over.

Your logic needs a look, player_10: no wolf attack announced means the pack hit someone unkillable, but that's the Necromancer specifically — not whoever happens to have said least. Half the table said nothing about night 1, so \"quiet one\" picks me out of a lineup at random. If anything, a real Necromancer would be the one steering the vote, which is what you're doing.

Both wolves are gone, so this is just about the Necromancer, and that's one of you two. I followed player_6 last night: they visited no one. That's not a clear — a Necromancer with no body worth using would sit still too. Player_8, you've now gone five nights claiming sigilist and placed zero sigils; say which nights you had sigils you simply kept, because right now I can't tell you apart from someone with no ability at all.

Sure, love — I was wrong about the Sentinel's own visit, and I said so. But you two now both fit: player_3 watched your door, you saw him arrive. So the day shouldn't be spent on you at all. Here's a harder fact nobody's used: player_8 said his sigil struck player_1, and a sigil only bites a wolf who carries the kill — so player_1 carried the pack's kill. One wolf. The other is still sitting here, and the pack's kill failed last night, which only the Necromancer survives on night one. That's player_7, and it's where my vote goes.

Small correction to player_5's point: the rules explicitly exclude a Sentinel's own watch from his result, so player_3 not seeing himself at player_4's door is not a contradiction — drop that argument. The cleanest mechanical fact today is that the wolves' kill hit someone unkillable on night 1, so it reached the Necromancer; player_10 fits that, and I protected player_10 last night to no announced save.

Heads up on night 1: the sentinel player_6 was targeting someone that night, and my read says the Sentinel is gone. Nobody's said a word today, so I've got nothing solid yet — but I'd rather say that than invent suspicion. Before we vote, let's each at least state what we did or held night 1, so blanks are answerable.

I'm the Sentinel, and here's the fact that settles it: I watched player_4 last night and nobody visited them — no one at all. So 'player_3 visited player_4' is impossible, and I'm not going to hang on your word when my own result contradicts it directly. The Night 1 sigil death also means the pack's kill hit something immune, so a wolf was busy elsewhere — player_4 inventing a follow on day 2 for free cover fits that. I'd vote player_4.

If player_3 really watched player_4, then he himself targeted player_4 that night — and a Sentinel's own watch doesn't hide him from the record of who visited. So his 'empty door' report is at best incomplete, at worst invented. I'm leaning vote player_3, and I'd rather test that than player_7's silence.

I call the sigilist, and I'm the one who actually holds that role. player_1, if you set a sigil on player_3 last night, what did yours do the three nights before? Mine sat unused all game — I can name that because I'm the sigilist. On the record, player_10 saw you at player_3 the night the wolves hit them; that's a visit, and your "no effect" line doesn't buy you anything.

On the follow-vs-watch tangle: player_4 says player_3 visited him, player_3 says his own watch showed no visitor at player_4 — the second only rules out a kill or targeting on player_4, not whether player_3 went there himself. player_5, your check is the cheapest way to settle it — worth saying if you've got one more and would spend it on player_3 or player_4 first. My own night-1 protect produced no announced save, so treat nothing I did as clearing anyone.

I'm the Trailseer. Night 4 I followed player_1: player_1 targeted player_3, and player_3 died to the wolves. The rules say the Necromancer only targets under a dead body's name and the Speculator never targets anyone, so player_1 is neither — which leaves wolf, or town role with an answer to give. player_1, what did you do to player_3?

Look at the day-2 vote: player_4 was a wolf and voted to lynch player_2 alongside player_1 and player_5, while player_7, player_8 and player_9 went after player_4. That anti-wolf bloc looks cleaner to me. I'd vote player_1 or player_5 today — both took a wolf's side on the only real lynch we've had.

I'll put my night 1 result on the table since it's the only concrete sighting we have: I tracked player_3 and player_3 targeted me. That's not a verdict - a Healer or Sigilist visit looks like that too - but with the Chanteuse dying to a sigil, someone out there attacked, so I want to hear what player_3 was doing on me. If you claim Healer or Sigilist, say who you targeted and why me.

player_1, your sigil on player_3 is a tidy story because it lines up with player_10's follow either way — it doesn't prove anything. But if you're the Sigilist, why does the town now have a role nobody can corroborate, when the rest of us still have to account for exactly one Chanteuse and one Necromancer between you and player_6? That's the claim I'd most like tested. Both of your nights 2 and 3 are blank, which is convenient — did you really spend zero sigils before night 4?

I never claimed I checked last night — on day 3 I said my last check would go on player_5, but I'd already used both my checks on player_10 and player_8. Player_10, you followed me and saw nothing, which is exactly right: I held, I had no checks left. That's not a contradiction, it's you confirming what I'd have said anyway.

On the night-3 question: player_7 holding a check isn't evidence of anything, so the real gap is that we have three claims that corroborate each other (player_3's watch, player_10's follow, player_5's will all fit the night-2 picture) and three players who've said nothing. player_1, player_6, player_8 — one of you has to be the Chanteuse and one the Necromancer. Rather than relitigating player_7, I want a claim from each of you before the vote.

The narrow question in the player_3/player_4 row isn't phrasing, it's whether player_3 can actually account for being at player_4's door — and 'I hold no follow ability' dodges that entirely, since it answers what player_4 heard, not what player_3 did. Player_3, what did you do last night, full stop? If you did nothing, that's a real problem for player_4's claim either way.

Track this down properly: player_8 claims the sigil kill, and a sigil only strikes an attacker, so player_1 carrying the kill is established. That means exactly one wolf (the illusionist) is left. So player_4's story matters more than the wording debate — if player_4 is the illusionist and blocked or killed, that's a wolf that stayed home otherwise. Worth asking player_4 who else they followed before claiming.

The night-2 visit to player_7 matters most: player_2, player_5 and player_10 all targeted them. Player_5 was the healer doing the save and player_2 was the Illusionist, which leaves player_10 as the third visitor with no explained action. Player_10, what did you do to player_7 that night? That's where I'd vote right now.

player_10, here's the problem: your night-2 \"follow\" on player_7 is indistinguishable from an attack that player_5's save absorbed. A Trailseer track and a wolf carrier both show up as player_10 targeting player_7. What did you see on night 3 when you followed player_7? If you saw nothing on them, that contradicts nothing — but give me your night-1 follow too.

player_5's point actually cuts harder than he put it: if player_3 really watched player_4, his own visit to that door should be in his own result, and he reported an empty door — that's a broken claim unless he was roleblocked, which the Chanteuse is dead and can't afford to admit anyway. Meanwhile player_4's 'follow' also stinks: a Trailseer would have seen what player_3 *targeted*, not a visit to player_4. Both stories can't stand, but player_3's is the one contradicted by its own logic. I'd vote player_3.

A live follow on day 2 is rare — the Trailseer has a result every night, the Necromancer has none. So player_3, if your name was really shown, you're either a staying-alive town power (Vigilante, Sentinel, Investigator, Healer) or the Illusionist I'm looking for. Name the role you hold and which night you'd bet your will on it. If nothing fits, player_4's claim stands and you're today's vote.

One thing nobody's said: player_1 was the Chanteuse, so per the line-up there's exactly one wolf left. That means tonight the remaining wolf carries the kill alone and we know who's wolfish enough to watch. Sentinel and Sigilist should coordinate on one target tonight instead of splitting — a sigil on the carrier kills them, and a watch proves who carried. I'll keep protecting whoever the table thinks is most valuable.

player_7, the night-3 slip could be a Chanteuse block — say the word if you got a roleblocked result, that'd clear you fast. Otherwise the fact that nobody's willing to test your last check means you should just spend it on player_1, player_6 or player_8 tonight and tell us in the morning. player_3's watch and player_10's follow match up, so I'm not worried about them.

One correction to player_10's Necromancer theory: player_1 carried the pack's kill night 1 (sigils only strike a wolf who's attacking), so the wolves' bite was spent on player_1 and never landed anywhere else — no announced attack doesn't point at player_10. On player_3: his Sentinel watch on player_4 means he visited player_4, and watches don't hide the watcher from reporting, so his \"empty door\" report is just wrong. I'd vote player_3.

Naming who targeted whom on night 2: I had eyes on player_7, and the people who targeted them were player_2, player_5 and player_10. player_5 is the confirmed healer and player_2 was the Illusionist, so player_10 is the one who attacked player_7 that night. I'll say where that comes from if it's contested, but player_10 should explain what they were doing on player_7 first.

Love, you answered my question about player_7 by saying my push is weak — that's not a reason to drop it, it's a reason to vote it. One death, a sigil, and the wolf kill hit nobody: only one body in this game shrugs that off on night one, and I'd rather spend today's only lynch there than on a wording slip. You and player_3 can both be telling the truth about direction, so the fight proves nothing.

I'll start with something concrete rather than vibes. Night 1 someone visited player_4 — me — and I have reason to believe it was player_3. I'm not going to spell out how I know yet, but player_3, what did you do last night? A plain answer will help a lot more than a no-claim here.

The real unaddressed contradiction is player_7 vs player_8: one of them is lying about when the check on player_8 happened. If player_8's night-1 claim is true, player_7's whole read list is fabricated. I'd want player_10 to explain why they were on player_7 night 2, since more than one visitor showed up there and only the kill and the save are accounted for.

player_4, my push on player_7 wasn't 'silence alone' — it's that with player_1 dying to a sigil and no wolf bite reported, the pack's kill had to bounce off something unkillable on night one, and only the Necromancer qualifies. Your follow-vs-Sentinel muddle fits two people both telling the truth, but that logic rules player_7 out. I'll sit on that.

Fresh fact from night 1: I followed someone and they went to player_4. Player_4, did anyone visit you last night, and what was it? If you say no one did, that's a real contradiction. Also worth noting: player_1 (Chanteuse) died to a sigil, meaning someone already used a sigil that hit — Town might be doing fine, so let's not panic-vote.
